items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    In the industrially important Chlor‐Alkali process, the chlorine evolution reaction (CER) over a ruthenium dioxide (RuO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ) catalyst competes with the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). This selectivity issue is elucidated on the microscopic level with the single‐crystalline model electrode RuO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    (110) by employing density functional theory (DFT) calculations in combination with the concept of volcano plots. We demonstrate that one monolayer of TiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    (110) supported on RuO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    (110) enhances the selectivity towards the CER by several orders of magnitudes, while preserving the high activity for the CER. This win‐win situation is attributed to the different slopes of the volcano curves for the CER and OER.
                  </jats:p>
title:
Controlling Selectivity in the Chlorine Evolution Reaction over RuO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    ‐Based Catalysts

items.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Current progress in modern electrocatalysis research is spurred by theory, frequently based on ab initio thermodynamics, where the stable reaction intermediates at the electrode surface are identified, while the actual energy barriers are ignored. This approach is popular in that a simple tool is available for searching for promising electrode materials. However, thermodynamics alone may be misleading to assess the catalytic activity of an electrochemical reaction as we exemplify with the chlorine evolution reaction (CER) over a RuO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>(110) model electrode. The full procedure is introduced, starting from the stable reaction intermediates, computing the energy barriers, and finally performing microkinetic simulations, all performed under the influence of the solvent and the electrode potential. Full kinetics from first‐principles allows the rate‐determining step in the CER to be identified and the experimentally observed change in the Tafel slope to be explained.</jats:p>
title: Full Kinetics from First Principles of the Chlorine Evolution Reaction over a RuO<sub>2</sub>(110) Model Electrode
